title: When Do Typed Decision Models Work in Transportation? Evidence from Travel Choice and Traffic Signal Control
abstract: arXiv:2611.22926v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Typed decision models combine natural-language understanding with a structured interface that returns a selected action and an option-level probability distribution without generating lengthy textual responses. Their low inference cost and response latency make them attractive for transportation problems with predefined alternatives. This paper investigates their effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency in two representative transportation tasks: individual travel-mode choice prediction and sequential traffic signal control. We systematically evaluate TypeSafe Jev and GPT-6 Luna Decisions against conventional transportation methods, reinforcement learning algorithms, and four chat-based large language models. translated_title: 类型化决策模型何时在交通领域有效？来自出行选择与交通信号控制的证据
translated_abstract: 类型化决策模型将自然语言理解与结构化接口相结合，在不生成冗长文本回复的情况下返回所选动作以及选项级别的概率分布。其低推理成本和响应延迟使其对于具有预定义备选方案的交通问题颇具吸引力。本文研究了这类模型在两个代表性交通任务中的有效性、鲁棒性和效率：个体出行方式选择预测和序贯交通信号控制。我们系统地将TypeSafe Jev和GPT-6 Luna Decisions与传统交通方法、强化学习算法以及四个基于对话的大语言模型进行了对比评估。在Swissmetro数据集上的实验表明，类型化决策模型的预测准确率低于传统离散选择模型和最强的基于对话的基线模型，且其性能存在显著差异。
tldr: 该论文系统评估了类型化决策模型在出行方式选择预测与交通信号控制两类交通任务中的表现，发现在Swissmetro数据集上其预测准确率低于传统离散选择模型和最强的对话式大语言模型基线，表明此类模型的有效性高度依赖于具体任务类型。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically evaluates typed decision models on travel-mode choice prediction and traffic signal control, finding that on the Swissmetro dataset they achieve lower prediction accuracy than traditional discrete choice models and the strongest chat-based baseline, indicating their effectiveness is highly task-dependent.
